meta.title: Malaysian elections
sources: Wikipedia: Malayan and Malaysian general election articles 1955–2022 (results, infoboxes and leads)

eras.label: Malaya before and after Merdeka
eras.blurb: The 1955 election, held two years before independence, gave the Alliance of UMNO, MCA and MIC 51 of 52 seats and made Tunku Abdul Rahman chief minister of a country that did not yet exist. The 1959 vote was the first of independent Malaya.

eras.label: Alliance high tide and 13 May
eras.blurb: The Alliance dominated the new Malaysia's first election in 1964, fought under Confrontation with Indonesia. The 1969 election broke the pattern: the opposition's surge was answered by the May 13 riots, a state of emergency and nearly two years of rule by decree before parliament returned.

eras.label: The Barisan Nasional decades
eras.blurb: Rebuilt as the Barisan Nasional, the ruling coalition won a two-thirds supermajority in every election for three decades. The votes were real and the counts broadly honest, but malapportionment, a controlled press and the Internal Security Act kept the contest tilted far toward the government — the Mahathir era at its peak delivered 1995's record landslide, and 2004's was larger still.

eras.label: The two-coalition era
eras.blurb: The 2008 'political tsunami' broke the two-thirds majority; in 2013 the BN kept power while losing the popular vote outright. In 2018 Malaysia's first change of government at the ballot box ended 61 years of continuous rule, and the hung parliament of 2022 produced Anwar Ibrahim's unity government — the contest is now genuinely national and genuinely uncertain.

elections.summary: General elections were held in the Federation of Malaya on Wednesday, 27 July 1955, the only general election before independence in 1957. They were held to elect members of the Federal Legislative Council, whose members had previously been fully appointed by the British High Commissioner.
elections.caveat: A pre-independence election under British oversight, on a citizens-only franchise that enfranchised a fraction of the population.

elections.summary: General elections were held in the Federation of Malaya on Wednesday, 19 August 1959 for members of the first Parliament of the Federation of Malaya, the first parliamentary election in Malaya. It was the third national-wide election held in Malaya since the end of World War II.

General elections were held in Malaysia on Saturday, 25 April 1964, to elect members of the expanded Dewan Rakyat, the lower house of the bicameral Parliament of Malaysia. These were the first federal elections since the Malaysia Agreement of 1963, which transformed the Federation of Malaya into Malaysia with the addition of Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak.
elections.caveat: Cleanly counted but heavily tilted: severe malapportionment, government-controlled media and the Internal Security Act framed every contest of the Barisan Nasional decades.

elections.summary: General elections were held in Malaysia on Saturday, 10 May 1969, although polling in Sabah and Sarawak was postponed until between 6 June and 4 July 1970. This was the first parliamentary election in Sabah and Sarawak since the formation of Malaysia in 1963.
elections.caveat: The results stood, but the aftermath did not: the May 13 riots led to a state of emergency, parliament suspended for 22 months, and voting in Sabah and Sarawak halted mid-election.

elections.summary: General elections were held in Malaysia between Saturday, 24 August and Saturday, 14 September 1974. Voting took place in all 154 parliamentary constituencies of Malaysia, each electing one Member of Parliament to the Dewan Rakyat, the dominant house of Parliament.
elections.caveat: Cleanly counted but heavily tilted: severe malapportionment, government-controlled media and the Internal Security Act framed every contest of the Barisan Nasional decades.

elections.knownAs: Won the vote, lost the power
elections.summary: General elections were held in Malaysia on Sunday, 5 May 2013. Voting took place in all 222 parliamentary constituencies, each electing one MP to the Dewan Rakyat, the dominant house of Parliament.
elections.caveat: The Barisan Nasional kept its majority while losing the popular vote 47–51 — the starkest product of Malaysia's malapportioned map.

elections.summary: General elections were held in Malaysia on Wednesday, 9 May 2018. At stake were all 222 seats in the Dewan Rakyat, the lower house of parliament.
General elections were held in Malaysia on Saturday, 19 November 2022.
